subject: Aurion Health — Pilot hold-open request while PO clears
messages:
From: Sean O'Neill <sean.oneill@aurionhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurements@aurionhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-11T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot hold-open request while PO clears

Hi Aditya / Lauren,

Quick update from procurement: our finance team approved the spend for the pilot last week but the PO is still routing through an external vendor verification step. That process unexpectedly added another review queue and we now expect the PO to clear in ~2–3 weeks.

We have an active pilot with your account that the product team is using heavily; we really want to keep momentum (and the evaluation metrics we shared earlier). Would Redwood be able to keep the sandbox/pilot environment active for an extra 21 days while the PO finalizes? If you need anything from our side I can push procurement to prioritize.

I can share a brief status memo from procurement if that helps.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Product Manager
Aurion Health

Attachment: Aurion_PO_Status_Memo.pdf (1 page — procurement timeline)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Sean O'Neill <sean.oneill@aurionhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot hold-open request while PO clears

Sean —

Thanks for the heads up and for the procurement memo, that helps. We definitely want to avoid any loss of momentum on the pilot. Quick clarity on our side: our standard self-serve sandbox sessions expire automatically after 7 days of inactivity, but for sales-led pilots we can offer a temporary hold-open with constrained credits while PO is in flight.

Options we can offer immediately while procurement finalizes:
- 7-day hold-open with full sandbox access (no contract required)
- 21-day constrained hold-open (reduced concurrent model capacity and an engagement cap) — this requires a short SLA-exception form signed so we can reserve capacity and ensure it doesn't impact other customers

If you can sign the SLA-exception and confirm the PO expected clearance date, we can provision the 21-day option today and attach it to deal RDW-ACME-2027-0193. If procurement is likely to clear sooner, the 7-day option is the fastest.

I copied Priyom and Lauren from post-sales to help with the SLA form and capacity configuration.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Sean / Maria —

Appreciate the procurement transparency and the PO target date. We've reviewed capacity and can do the 21-day hold-open under these quick terms:

- Duration: 21 days (2027-04-14 through 2027-05-05)
- Credits: 25k token-equivalent soft cap, throttled to prevent burst to production-grade GPUs
- Access: sandbox environment only (no dedicated instance); we will enable model variants M-alpha-1 (quantized) to reduce cost impact
- SLA form: please sign the attached one-page SLA-exception that documents the cap and confirms the PO target date
- Next steps: Maria, please return the signed SLA-exception to priyom_das@redwood.ai and we will provision the hold-open within 24 business hours.

I've attached the SLA-exception template and a short operational note on the throttling so your engineers know what to expect. If you prefer, we can also provision a short-term dedicated queue for an additional fee — happy to discuss if your team wants guaranteed throughput instead.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference
